definitions.explanation: A bomb that releases energy through nuclear fission or fusion, capable of massive destruction. An umbrella term covering both {原子爆弾|げんしばくだん} ('atomic bomb') and {水素爆弾|すいそばくだん} ('hydrogen bomb').

examples.japanese: {核爆弾|かくばくだん}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{脅威|きょうい}→脅威：13932_kyoui⟧。
{核爆弾|かくばくだん}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{使用|しよう}→使用：01637_shiyou⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{決|けっ}して→決して：01254_kesshite⟧⟦{許|ゆる}されない→許す：02325_yurusu⟧。
examples.english: The use of nuclear bombs must never be permitted.

examples.japanese: {冷戦|れいせん}⟦{時代|じだい}→時代：01424_jidai⟧、⟦{両国|りょうこく}→両国：10010_ryoukoku⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{大量|たいりょう}→大量：03112_tairyou⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{核爆弾|かくばくだん}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{保有|ほゆう}→保有：11615_hoyuu⟧⟦していた→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: During the Cold War, both countries possessed large numbers of nuclear bombs.

examples.japanese: ⟦{国際|こくさい}→国際：01406_kokusai⟧⟦{社会|しゃかい}→社会：01427_shakai⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{核爆弾|かくばくだん}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{廃絶|はいぜつ}→廃絶：28187_haizetsu⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{向|む}けて→向ける：02306_mukeru⟧⟦{努力|どりょく}→努力：03490_doryoku⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{続|つづ}け→続く：00903_tsuzuku⟧て⟦いる→いる：00495_iru⟧。
examples.english: The international community continues its efforts toward the abolition of nuclear bombs.

notes:
Compound of ⟦{核|かく}→核：13127_kaku⟧ ('nucleus; nuclear') and ⟦{爆弾|ばくだん}→爆弾：10117_bakudan⟧ ('bomb'). ⟦{核|かく}→核：13127_kaku⟧ prefixes a wide range of nuclear-related terms: ⟦{核兵器|かくへいき}→核兵器：13126_kakuheiki⟧ ('nuclear weapon'), {核実験|かくじっけん} ('nuclear test'), {核廃絶|かくはいぜつ} ('nuclear abolition').

USAGE:
Used in news reporting, political discussion, and historical writing about nuclear weapons. In contemporary public discourse in Japan — where the atomic bombings of Hiroshima and Nagasaki are a foundational memory — ⟦{核|かく}→核：13127_kaku⟧-related vocabulary carries strong moral weight. The abolitionist phrase ⟦{核|かく}→核：13127_kaku⟧⟦{廃絶|はいぜつ}→廃絶：28187_haizetsu⟧ appears frequently.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {核爆弾|かくばくだん}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{脅威|きょうい}→脅威：13932_kyoui⟧: the threat of nuclear bombs
- {核爆弾|かくばくだん}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{保有|ほゆう}→保有：11615_hoyuu⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧: to possess nuclear bombs
- {核爆弾|かくばくだん}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{投下|とうか}→投下：12893_touka⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧: to drop a nuclear bomb
- {核爆弾|かくばくだん}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{開発|かいはつ}→開発：06746_kaihatsu⟧: development of nuclear bombs
- {核爆弾|かくばくだん}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{廃絶|はいぜつ}→廃絶：28187_haizetsu⟧: abolition of nuclear bombs
- {核爆弾|かくばくだん}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{実験|じっけん}→実験：03273_jikken⟧: testing of nuclear bombs

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{核兵器|かくへいき}→核兵器：13126_kakuheiki⟧: nuclear weapon — broader term including missiles and warheads, not just bombs
- ⟦{原子爆弾|げんしばくだん}→原子爆弾：22697_genshibakudan⟧: atomic bomb — fission bomb; the Hiroshima/Nagasaki type (abbreviated ⟦{原爆|げんばく}→原爆：11942_genbaku⟧)
- {水素爆弾|すいそばくだん}: hydrogen bomb — fusion bomb (abbreviated {水爆|すいばく})
- ⟦{核弾頭|かくだんとう}→核弾頭：23262_kakudantou⟧: nuclear warhead — the nuclear payload of a missile
- {核実験|かくじっけん}: nuclear test

CULTURAL NOTE:
Japan is the only country to have been attacked with atomic bombs (Hiroshima and Nagasaki, 1945), which has given the topic of nuclear weapons special moral significance in Japanese society. The phrase 'the only atomically bombed nation' (⟦{唯一|ゆいいつ}→唯一：01666_yuiitsu⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{被爆国|ひばくこく}) is often invoked in discussions of nuclear policy and disarmament.
